item.title: Steam's Biggest Stardew Valley-Like RPG Was Just Delayed to 2027, and It Hurts
item.description:
While there are quite a few games I've been looking forward to in 2026—including The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake and Grand Theft Auto 6 —one of my most anticipated games this year was none other than Emberville , an RPG that has been described as a cross between Stardew Valley and Diablo . As a massive fan of both Stardew Valley and Diablo , as well as Emberville 's stellar and recognizable voice cast, I have been anxiously awaiting its initial October 27, 2026 Steam Early Access release date. At the time of writing, that day is tomorrow, so imagine my sadness when I read today that Emberville has been delayed to January 2027. If you've also been waiting for the release of what looks like one of the most promising indie games in recent memory, then maybe we can just be sad together.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Fortunately, Emberville is still on the way, even if we have to wait a bit longer for it to be released. Since that's not the case for every upcoming game these days, with studios closing and games being canceled left and right, I'm still thankful I'll get to play it at some point. Plus, I'm all for delays if that's what a developer needs to make their game even better. In fact, that's precisely why Cygnus Cross, Emberville 's developer, chose to delay the game in the first place. According to a post made by the developer today on Emberville 's official X account, Cygnus Cross stated that they recognized the room the game has left for improvement, and they wanted to delay the game to fill in that gap. More than likely, after Emberville 's Steam Next Fest demo went live, the team received feedback that made them feel more comfortable about waiting until 2027 to launch the game—but it still hurts.

New Open-World Game Is Like Pokemon Meets Stardew Valley, and It Has 10/10 Reviews

A new open-world game on Steam earns rave reviews from players, making it a perfect pick for fans of Pokemon and Stardew Valley.

By Mohsen Baqery

Emberville Has Been Delayed to January 2027, and With It, My Excitement

Funny enough, I actually came really close to downloading Emberville 's demo during Steam Next Fest, but ultimately decided against it. Not because I wasn't interested, obviously, but because I figured I'd rather wait until the game entered Early Access and experience everything for the first time then. After all, I was only going to have to wait a few more days, and I knew that if I enjoyed the demo as much as I expected to, I'd probably just end up wishing I could keep playing. And as much as I could download and play it before Steam Next Fest ends, I don't think I want to at this point. I'd rather just wait.

Wishlist Today

For those unfamiliar with Emberville , the game begins with players waking up without their memories in a massive underground prison known as the Vitromotus. From there, they'll fight monsters, explore dungeons, and rescue survivors who can help them rebuild the ruined town of Emberville. It honestly sounds like the perfect combination of some of my favorite games, especially when you consider just how many different activities there are to get lost in.

Emberville Key Features

  • ACTION RPG COMBAT – Fight monsters using different weapons, spells, and abilities.
  • CLASS CUSTOMIZATION – Combine abilities from different classes to create unique builds.
  • TOWN REBUILDING – Rescue villagers and help bring Emberville back to life.
  • FARMING AND COOKING – Grow crops, collect ingredients, and prepare meals.
  • DUNGEON EXPLORATION – Explore dangerous areas filled with monsters, bosses, and loot.
  • CHARACTER RELATIONSHIPS – Get to know the villagers and uncover their stories.

As a longtime fan of games like Stardew Valley and Diablo , I can't help but get excited about all of that. I love the idea of spending hours fighting monsters and collecting loot, only to return home and spend just as much time farming, cooking, or getting to know the people I've rescued. And considering that Emberville also features a voice cast that includes Matthew Mercer, Jennifer English, and Ben Starr, I'm especially interested in seeing how much depth its characters and story have.

However, after looking into what players have been saying about Emberville 's Steam Next Fest demo, I can at least understand why Cygnus Cross decided to delay it. Some players have praised the game's art style, voice acting, and combat systems, while others have been considerably less enthusiastic about their experience. In particular, I've seen complaints about the combat feeling clunky, with players criticizing how movement is restricted during attacks. Others have reported problems with bow accuracy, controller support, and inventory management. I've even seen some disappointment over the fact that the demo doesn't really show off the farming and town-building activities that make the game so appealing in the first place.

Hopefully, Emberville's Delay Will Be Worth the Wait

Obviously, I can't speak from personal experience about any of those issues, since I never actually played the demo myself, but I'm glad Cygnus Cross is apparently taking the feedback seriously. In fact, the developer has specifically mentioned reworking bow combat as one of the reasons for the delay, and some content originally planned for Emberville 's first major Early Access update will now be included when the game launches. I'd say that's a pretty good consolation prize, especially if the extra time also allows the team to address some of the frustrations players have been reporting.

Steam's Biggest Stardew Valley-Like RPG Was Just Delayed to 2027, and It Hurts
'Brutally Challenging' 2D Platformer Game on Steam Is Now Permanently Free
New Sim Game is Basically Dungeons & Dragons Meets Fallout Shelter
Phantom Blade Zero Already Hits Massive Milestone

But man, I really wanted to play Emberville this year. And while I'm certainly disappointed that I won't be able to, I also don't want to see a game with this much potential stumble simply because it wasn't quite ready. I've been looking forward to it for far too long to let a couple of extra months change that, and honestly, I'd rather wait for a better experience than get my hands on something that might leave me disappointed. So, January 7, 2027 it is. I just really wish I could be playing it tomorrow instead.

Emberville

item.title: 5 Open-World RPGs That Make Skyrim's Exploration Feel Limited, Ranked
item.description:
I think most of us could agree that The Elder Scrolls 5: Skyrim is one of the most influential open-world RPGs ever created, and I definitely understand why so many people keep replaying it. It has a huge world full of interesting locations and, honestly, plenty of opportunities to get yourself in trouble. Undoubtedly, it is an extremely impressive title and offers some of the best exploration in the genre.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

However, some open-world RPGs have surpassed it, and interestingly, not in terms of having bigger maps or more places to visit. Some make navigating unfamiliar territory a challenge all its own, while others reward curiosity by allowing you to completely change how you approach the game; in any case, the exploration in these games is just spectacular .

5 Fallout: New Vegas

Exploration That Changes The Political Landscape

Fallout: New Vegas is all about the conflict between several factions competing for control: the New California Republic, Caesar's Legion, and Mr. House. Skyrim also features political conflict between the Imperial Legion and the Stormcloaks, but the difference between the two games is in how extensively these conflicts influence your exploration. In Fallout: New Vegas , discovering new settlements and military outposts allows players to explore the different perspectives of the region's political powers. Moreover, your decisions can influence your relationships with the factions involved.

Find all 10 pairs

Results

0
—
More Games

While in Skyrim the Civil War also affects certain settlements and their leadership, the game's exploration experience is far less dependent on your political allegiance. This basically means that exploring new locations rarely changes how opposing factions treat you. Many would agree that experiencing the consequences of your actions is what makes exploration in Fallout: New Vegas more rewarding, especially because it makes the experience more realistic.

Another advantage of Fallout: New Vegas is the way geography influences travel. Approaching New Vegas is extremely dangerous for inexperienced characters because of the Deathclaws lurking around Quarry Junction and Cazadores. This encourages players to take longer routes if they want to survive. Skyrim also features dangerous enemies, but its level scaling makes exploration more forgiving. Fallout: New Vegas gives players more opportunities to think about their strategy, figure out where they stand in terms of how strong they are, and generally plan safer routes instead of simply going forward.

4 Dragon's Dogma 2

A World With Dangerous Journeys

Dragon's Dogma 2 follows the story of the Arisen, and unlike Skyrim , where players can fast travel to most locations, this game relies on Ferrystones, Portcrystals, and oxcarts. These means of transportation have restrictions, of course, and players must actually stop and consider how they are going to move from point A to point B. Implementing strategy when it comes to traveling is a great way to make the experience more interesting and, generally, way more rewarding, because even revisiting familiar areas requires some preparation.

5 Turn-Based RPGs With Virtually Perfect Class Systems

As turn-based RPGs often live and die on their class systems, these games lived their absolute best lives.

By Mark Sammut

Moreover, nighttime also has a big influence on the way players experience exploration. Skyrim also features dangerous creatures after sunset, but in Dragon's Dogma 2 , visibility is also severely reduced, so lanterns are essential, especially if you are walking on unfamiliar roads. This is usually where players have to consider whether they want to continue traveling or play it safe and set up a campsite, which adds another layer of complexity.

Both games feature random encounters and attacks, but Dragon's Dogma 2 also allows players to climb onto enemies and exploit their weaknesses during combat. This makes encounters more interactive than just using ordinary weapon attacks. Last but not least, it's important to mention the Pawn system that gives companions an active role in exploration. Skyrim also has Followers, but Pawns can share knowledge of locations, quests, and other resources acquired during previous adventures, which makes them extremely useful as companions for navigation as well as in combat.

Dragon's Dogma 2

3 The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind

Greater Freedom Without Constant Directions

Most who have ever played The Elder Scrolls 3: Morrowind end up falling in love with the game. The story takes place on a volcanic island filled with ancient ruins, huge mushrooms, and settlements of different cultures. Generally, it requires players to follow directions provided by NPCs to find quest objectives, rather than relying on quest markers as they would in Skyrim . You actually have to investigate your surroundings rather than follow an icon on the map.

I personally find Morrowind 's approach to exploration far more engaging when I have to use the roads, landmarks, or other geographical peculiarities to guide me. Moreover, Morrowind features Levitation spells that allow you to fly around, while Mark and Recall provide customizable teleportation. Skyrim doesn't have any comparable abilities, so you actually are way more limited when it comes to moving around. You get a lot more creative freedom in Morrowind because you aren't limited to walking on the ground.

Generally, the geography in Morrowind is way more interesting to investigate because of its volcanic wastelands, giant mushrooms, and distinctive architecture. It's true that Skyrim also features varied landscapes, but Morrowind has a kind of alien setting which, combined with its navigation mechanics, simply creates an amazing exploration experience.

The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind

2 Outward

Exploration Is A Genuine Survival Challenge

One of my favorite things about Outward is that its map doesn't show exactly where your character is. While Skyrim displays the player's position and provides quest markers, in Outward , players have to identify landmarks themselves and compare their surroundings with the map to determine their location. This makes exploration far more engaging because getting lost is actually a possibility, and successfully navigating unfamiliar territory means that you have to pay attention. It's kind of like using Google Maps in real life. At some point, you find yourself simply following the blue arrow without paying attention to your surroundings at all, and if somebody asks you for directions later, you don't even remember how you reached your destination.

10 Open-World Games That Refuse To Hold Your Hand (No Markers, No Tutorials)

Open-world gaming is better without quest markers or tutorials. These games challenge you to rely on your own instincts and curiosity to succeed.

9
By Evan Regan

Moreover, Outward's survival mechanics contribute to a better exploration experience because players must manage their hunger, thirst, exhaustion, and even diseases. Skyrim also has an optional Survival Mode, but Outward integrates these mechanics into the core gameplay. This adds another layer of complexity to the game and makes it way more engaging, not to mention that reaching distant locations becomes way more satisfying because of the challenge involved in getting there.

Last but not least, the way Outward handles defeat actually makes exploring dangerous territories way more consequential. Instead of just reloading after losing a fight, you might find yourself in prison or robbed and left for dead. This makes exploration way more unpredictable than Skyrim 's, which I find quite exciting.

1 Elden Ring

A World That Constantly Rewards Your Curiosity

Elden Ring is one of my favorite games in the entire world. It takes place in the Lands Between, a ruined fantasy kingdom filled with enemies, civilizations, and all kinds of secret locations. One of its greatest advantages over Skyrim is the vertical complexity of its open world. It features enormous subterranean regions like Siofra River and Nokron, Eternal City, which are located beneath places that you have already visited. This gives you a way stronger incentive to investigate every corner of the map.

8 Most Open RPGs Of All Time

Open-world RPGs are one of the most popular genres in modern gaming, and these games take the concept of "open exploration" very seriously.

1
By Mark Sammut

Moreover, dungeons in Elden Ring don't follow the same straightforward routes that Skyrim 's dungeons do. They feature interconnected passages, rooftops, hidden rooms, and even alternative paths. This makes exploration not only fun but also important, because the environment can help you avoid dangerous encounters.

Elden Ring also rewards exploration with some very impressive rewards. Finding certain items can introduce you to entirely new combat strategies, for example. Last but not least, Elden Ring has this tendency to hide important discoveries in seemingly insignificant locations. Skyrim certainly rewards your curiosity as well, but the scale of Elden Ring 's discoveries is much harder to predict.

item.title: 'Brutally Challenging' 2D Platformer Game on Steam Is Now Permanently Free
item.description:
Bounce Quest is a 2025 2D platformer on Steam that claims to be incredibly hard to beat, and it is now free for all users to try. The game launched on Steam with a $4.99 price tag, but it has recently joined the platform's lineup of free titles.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Developer Nozech describes Bounce Quest as "a brutally challenging platformer where you explore a treacherous mountain to uncover what lies at the top." Like some other nerve-racking climbing games, Bounce Quest comes with a catch: a fall can sometimes erase all the player's progress and set them far back.

9/10 Co-Op Shooter Game on Steam Is Now Permanently Free

A distinctive co-op shooter with overwhelmingly positive Steam reviews is now available at no cost, and anyone can download and enjoy it.

By Mohsen Baqery

Bounce Quest Became Free-to-Play on Steam on October 13

The developer has not disclosed why Bounce Quest dropped its $4.99 price tag. However, SteamDB data confirms that the change took effect on October 13. Bounce Quest has few user reviews on Steam, but the handful it has received seem incredibly positive. Some players have also suggested that it is indeed a challenging 2D platformer. One user wrote, "I can't say I enjoyed this one, and my desk had a hard time, but I definitely recommend checking it out."

In Bounce Quest , players control a bouncy cube whose main moves are jumping, sliding, and smashing. But the gameplay mostly depends on how they time their jumps, how far they jump, and where they land. The character's bouncy nature helps it clear obstacles, but it can also backfire and send it flying in the opposite direction. In other words, an ill-timed jump or rough landing can cause players to fall and lose progress. The developer also warns that "the higher you go, the harder you will fall."

Bounce Quest is not an arcade game where players only aim to score points by climbing as high as possible. The developer says a secret awaits at the top of the mountain that players are trying to climb. So, as its title suggests, Bounce Quest is a linear 2D platformer with six unique areas to explore. Players looking for extra content may also appreciate the dozen different skins they can unlock for the protagonist.

Steam users might also be interested to know that Bounce Quest isn't the only 2D platformer to recently become free. Another game, Jump Adventures , features similar gameplay and aesthetics and has also dropped its price on Steam. Together, the two titles offer hours of free content, especially for players who enjoy cozy-looking games that constantly push them to rage-quit. Those looking for a more arcade-style experience, however, can check out Cartomancy Anthology on Steam, another paid game that recently became free. Cartomancy Anthology is a collection of more than 20 small games, most of which offer a relaxed gameplay experience.

item.title: Rare Copy of Pokemon Red Sells for Over $100,000
item.description:
An unusually rare copy of Pokemon Red has sold for over $100,000 at auction. Given the recent sale, anyone who has a similar copy of Pokemon Red could end up with a small fortune, should they decide to sell it. However, this particular copy may be one-of-a-kind.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Rare Pokemon merchandise can fetch a pretty hefty sum these days, with rare Pokemon cards being some of the most expensive among them. While some of these cards have been drawn from standard packs, a number of them were rare to begin with, like the iconic Pikachu Illustrator card, which has sold for millions in the past. Such is also the case with this recently-sold copy of Pokemon Red , which was never available on a store shelf.

The 14 Rarest 3DS Games (& How Much They're Worth)

The Nintendo 3DS might be long gone, but its games live on. Some of them are also hard to find and expensive as heck to buy.

4
By Jeff Drake

Rare Pokemon Red Prototype Sells for Six Figures

On October 25, a Goldin auction for a prototype copy of Pokemon Red closed after receiving 20 bids and reaching a whopping $101,000 final winning bid. After fees, the cost for the cartridge reached $123,220. The prototype isn't much to look at, with no official branding or external packaging, with the internal components of the cartridge fully visible. While PSA authentication determined that the cartridge is a prototype, a scan of the internal data didn't yield any differences between the game data on it and the standard US release of the game. There were apparently some minor differences located in the header data, but they were deemed "inconsequential." Not all of the data on the cartridge was accessible due to an "equipment failure," but the assessment determined that it's likely that the game build on the cartridge is identical to the official release.

Unfortunately, the assessment of the cartridge means that it's unlikely to yield any secrets from the development era of the game. Pre-release prototypes are often coveted in part because they sometimes have beta files in them that didn't make it to an official release copy. However, the cartridge still managed to net a sizable sum despite this knowledge being shared in the auction listing. It's nonetheless an interesting part of Pokemon history, and something that a collector will be able to consider largely one-of-a-kind, too, as no other instances of this particular development board have been documented in the past.

On the other hand, a completely non-functioning shell of a Nintendo GameCube that was put on display at SpaceWorld went on sale for $100,000.

item.title: Haunted Chocolatier's Best Marketing Trick Is What It Still Isn't Showing
item.description:
Haunted Chocolatier has been in development for years, but ConcernedApe has revealed relatively little about how the finished game will work. For the creator of Stardew Valley , that might seem like an unusual way to build hype. Most studios showcase as much gameplay as possible before launch, but I think holding back could work in Haunted Chocolatier 's favor. Leaving some mechanics unexplained gives players the chance to discover them for themselves, an experience that can get lost when games are extensively previewed before release.

Add GameRant on Google Add as Preferred Source Follow on Google Discover

Since announcing the game in 2021 (which, yes, was five years ago), Eric Barone, better known as ConcernedApe, has shared occasional glimpses of its development without explaining every system. That restraint can frustrate fans eager for more information, especially after such a long wait. Still, I'd rather discover an interesting mechanic while playing than have it explained in a trailer months before launch. The challenge is keeping that mystery alive without allowing the lack of updates to wear down the audience's enthusiasm.

Haunted Chocolatier's Best Dungeon Might Be Hiding in Its Chocolate Shop

Why Haunted Chocolatier’s chocolate shop might make every expedition matter in combat, crafting, and progression.

By Rain Egan

Haunted Chocolatier Will Benefit From Keeping Its Secrets

Part of the fun of starting a new game is figuring out how its systems work. An unexpected crafting recipe or a new way to interact with a character can change how players approach the world. Stardew Valley makes good use of this feeling, letting players gradually develop their own routines and discover how its activities fit together. I'd like Haunted Chocolatier to offer a similar experience rather than explain its most interesting mechanics before players can try them.

The premise already leaves room for surprises. Players will run a chocolate shop from a haunted castle, gathering ingredients and making sweets in a game that ConcernedApe has described as more action-focused than Stardew Valley . I'm interested in seeing how its systems work together, particularly as combat and exploration give the game a different feel from its predecessor. Discovering those connections firsthand could be far more satisfying than seeing every feature broken down in promotional footage.

Early Reveals Can Create Expectations

Game marketing often involves extended gameplay demonstrations, previews, and developer diaries long before release. While these can build excitement, they also create expectations around features that are still being developed. Once a mechanic appears in an official showcase, fans may grow attached to it, making later changes disappointing even when they improve the game.

ConcernedApe has explained his reluctance to reveal unfinished systems. In a June 2026 development update, he compared showing unfinished work to serving half-baked bread, saying he would rather present something complete. Systems can change considerably during development, and revealing them too early risks disappointing players when the final version differs. Keeping those details private gives him room to experiment without turning every early idea into a public promise.

The Risk of Keeping Fans Waiting

Mystery can only sustain interest for so long. Haunted Chocolatier was announced in 2021, and it still has no confirmed release date. ConcernedApe has continued working on Stardew Valley alongside his new project, but the extended development has left fans waiting years for substantial news. Occasional updates provide reassurance, yet long gaps can make even an enthusiastic audience lose momentum.

Players don't need to see every feature, but they do need reasons to remain interested. A new screenshot or short gameplay clip can demonstrate progress without spoiling major discoveries. ConcernedApe doesn't need a rigid marketing schedule, though sharing meaningful updates could help keep excitement alive. His August 2026 check-in acknowledged the difficulty of asking fans to remain patient, highlighting the challenge of balancing development freedom with audience expectations.

ConcernedApe Can Take a Different Approach

The success of Stardew Valley gives ConcernedApe an advantage. Haunted Chocolatier already has an audience eager to see what he creates, allowing him to take a less conventional approach to marketing. An unfamiliar indie game might need frequent showcases to stand out, but Barone's previous work has already given his next project considerable visibility.

I'd rather see him focus on making Haunted Chocolatier work than feel pressured to turn every development milestone into promotional material. That doesn't mean fans should have to wait indefinitely without updates. Sharing meaningful progress while keeping unfinished systems under wraps could help preserve the excitement of discovery without losing the audience along the way.

Haunted Chocolatier May Play an Opposite Role to Stardew Valley Among Cozy Sims

ConcernedApe's approach carries risks, particularly after years of development, but keeping some systems secret could make Haunted Chocolatier more rewarding to play. The game doesn't need to reveal every mechanic to maintain interest. It needs to offer enough reassurance that fans know development is progressing while leaving room for genuine surprises. If Barone strikes that balance, players may find that the best part of the wait is finally getting to discover the game for themselves.
